sections.causes:
The cause of Syphilis is mainly bacteria (Treponema pallidum) which spreads through sexual contact during vaginal, oral or anal sex. 
 This bacteria usually enters the body through minor cuts or is present in the inner moist lining of the body parts. 
 If the active sore is present on the lips, tongue or breasts can be easily spread through kissing or touching. 
 Treponema continuously spreads to the body and can eventually damage the organs. 
 Syphilis can’t be spread by Toilet seats, swimming pools, hot tubs, or eating utensils.
sections.symptoms:
The symptoms of Syphilis are divided into 3 stages which may vary and can overlap. Three stages of Syphilis are 
 1. Primary Syphilis 
 The first symptom of primary syphilis is the presence of a small sore which is known as Chancre which is a painless sore. 

 These sores are usually present on the genitals, anal and rectum region. 
 It is usually found between 10-90 days. 
 Primary syphilis sore heals without getting a scar within 6 weeks. 
 Sometimes, the only symptom of primary syphilis is swollen lymph nodes. 

 2. Secondary Syphilis 
 The symptoms of secondary syphilis appear when there is the healing of the first chancre. 

 These sores usually appear after 6 weeks and lasts for 1-3 month. 
 Secondary syphilis sores are usually rosy “copper penny” rashes, usually seen on the palms of hands and feet. 
 The sores are moist, wart-like lesions in the groin region, swollen lymph nodes and fever. 
 Sometimes, secondary syphilis is mistaken for conditions such as Pityriasis rosea, Psoriasis and Lichen Planus. 

 3. Tertiary Syphilis 
 The tertiary stage of syphilis is when the infection is not treated properly and it starts affecting the organs such as Heart, Brain and nerves. It can be deadly as it can lead to a person becoming paralysed, blind or deaf. 

 These sores usually appear after 6 weeks and lasts for 1-3 month. 
 Secondary syphilis sores are usually rosy “copper penny” rashes, usually seen on the palms of hands and feet. 
 The sores are moist, wart-like lesions in the groin region, swollen lymph nodes and fever. 
 Sometimes, secondary syphilis is mistaken for conditions such as Pityriasis rosea, Psoriasis and Lichen Planus.
